text: - P2200 cannot help: Pascal, no bf16, 5 GB < weights. Real lever = more RAM (16 GB DIMMs → 64-96 GB enables DS-V3.1-class 4-bit).
- Awaiting Bean's go to download + benchmark on a second port.
- 06:05 UTC: Daily digest posted — 2 sections with real links
- Control: 8k + --parallel 1 works, generates ~14 tok/s, survives.
- 16k default (CUDA0 KV offload) -> LOADS then DIES on first token. KV=4320 MiB (4096 CPU + 640 CUDA0) + 892 MiB compute buffer.
- 16k + `-nkvo` -> WORKS. KV stays in RAM, generates, survives. Free RAM after load ~6 GB.
- 24k + `-nkvo` -> short prompt works (14.3 tok/s), but a realistic 2k-token prompt killed it. Edge, not safe.
- 32k + `-nkvo` -> loads, DIES on first token. KV would be ~8.6 GB; too big for 24 GB box with 17.6 GB already used by 5001.
- Realistic 37.5k-char (~9.4k token) prompt at 16k: prefill slows 142->104->80->66->50 tok/s as cache fills, and the request blew past 240s. Prefill is the bottleneck, not VRAM.
- Verified live 5001 unaffected throughout; all probes killed, RAM back to ~13.1 GB used.
- CONCLUSION: 16k + -nkvo is the only safe upgrade on this box. 32k needs more RAM. q8_0 KV is not usable (FA disabled on Pascal P2200).

- Step 1 benchmark: GPU-resident KV (12k, --kv-offload) prefill 193 tok/s but decode 1.02 tok/s; -nkvo (32k) prefill 100 tok/s, decode 5.60 tok/s, 132.4s total. -ngl 99 impossible: 9,768 MiB on 5,120 MiB card. WINNER: -nkvo.
- Step 2 applied: deepseek-coder.service now `-c 32768 --parallel 1 --cont-batching -nkvo --spec-draft-ngl 99`. Live, n_ctx=32768.
- BORK: I first wrote `--nkvo` (invalid; correct is `-nkvo` / `--no-kv-offload`) -> auto-restart loop. Fixed. Backup: deepseek-coder.service.bak.1794640646
- Step 3: SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT 180->300, FETCH_EXCERPT_CHARS 10000->24000.

- REAL BUG FOUND: _local_summarize was one blocking call; 300s timeout threw away all generated text. Foreground repro: TimeoutError at exactly 300s while server still generating (task 10, 166 tok, 0.76 tok/s).
- FIX: rewrote _local_summarize to stream SSE (`"stream": True`), per-read timeout, keeps partial output as `[stream stopped: ...]`. Backup: /tmp/yt_transcript.py.bak.streaming

- Step 4 chunking: added CHUNK_CHARS=12000 and _split_chunks(); summarize_with_local_gpu now map-reduce (extract per chunk, tag PART i/N, merge, compress). Verified lossless: 27,022 chars -> [12000,12000,3022].

- KEY PERF FINDING: decode at high KV occupancy is ~0.7 tok/s vs ~14 tok/s cold-slot. A 24k-char excerpt with 900 max_tokens = ~20 min. Prefill is NOT the bottleneck (100-193 tok/s); DECODE is. My earlier "prefill is the ceiling" claim was wrong.
- STILL OPEN: single-pass vs chunked quality comparison. Single-pass run (task 182) in flight at 244 tok / 0.71 tok/s when session paused.

- **Decision lesson (2026-11-14, Option 3 rollout):** `systemctl start` on an already-active unit is a **no-op** — the old `-c 32768 -nkvo` kept serving for ~45 min while `/health` said OK, masking the config change. Caught it only by reading argv from `/proc/$(pgrep llama-server)/cmdline`. Rule: after any unit edit, use `restart` (not `start`) and verify effective flags from `/proc`, not from the health endpoint. Second lesson: decode speed tracks **KV occupancy**, not KV location — `-nkvo` and q8_0 KV are dead ends on Pascal P2200 (no Flash Attention). Tuning knob is chunk size, not context length. <!-- project: path:/home/rook/.openclaw/workspace -->

- **GPU ASR works on P2200 — faster-whisper, NOT whisper.cpp (10:00 UTC).** When YouTube timedtext is 429-blocked, download audio with a non-web player client (`--extractor-args youtube:player_client=default,-web`; only the *caption* endpoint is throttled, media is fine) and transcribe locally.

- **Do not build whisper.cpp here.** It compiled for >15 min and never finished: the CUDA path builds hundreds of MMQ template instances even with `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=ON`. Abandoned, artifacts removed.
- **Use `faster-whisper` in a venv** (`python3 -m venv /tmp/fw && /tmp/fw/bin/pip install faster-whisper`). `ctranslate2.get_cuda_device_count()` = 1.
- **`compute_type="float16"` FAILS on Pascal** — "target device or backend do not support efficient float16 computation." Use **`float32`**. (P2200 is CC 6.1, no bf16.)

- Measured on 18:48 of audio: `base.en` load 10s + transcribe 15.5s = **73x realtime**; `small.en` 19s + 41.1s = **27x**. Quality: small.en fixes "rebel capitals"→"rebel capitalists". Prefer small.en when accuracy matters, base.en when speed does.

- Also fixed a real `yt_transcript.py` bug: default `--lang` was `en`, but videos with no manual subs publish under `en-orig`, so the tool reported "no captions" when auto-captions existed. Default is now `en-orig,en`. <!-- project: path:/home/rook/.openclaw/workspace -->
